editorial_scope: First three reader essays select arguments from the prequel, Mutual Covenant and Mutual Questioning; they do not claim to translate every proposition or appendix.
All countries, events, speeches, dates and votes in the case world are fictional. No invented historical anecdotes or additional factual claims about actual states are added.
The absence of a common coercive superior defines the arrangement being investigated; it does not describe every existing international institution or forbid a voluntary political union.
National consent, individual dissent, equal institutional standing, and equal representation of persons are distinguished.
New obligations require relevant consent; previously accepted majority procedures and existing duties remain effective within their scope.
Withheld accession consent does not imply immunity for conduct under an existing obligation; the fertilizer contract is not asserted to prove a hidden bargain.
The questioner does not monopolize closure. Standing to ask, treaty duties to answer, opinions, judgments and enforcement remain distinct.
Policy changes following an inquiry are not asserted to have been caused by it. No report of retaliation is not verified absence of retaliation.
Affected people outside member territory can reach questions about the system's own measures; common procedure and national implementation retain separate responsibility.
Six planned essays are displayed as an unlinked reading plan, not falsely announced as published.
